When will I use this?

Estimation and rounding: when will I use this?

Whenever you need to know an answer looks right before you trust it.

Shop floor assistant

Sales, marketing and procurement

\(\displaystyle 19 \times 24 \approx 20 \times 24\)

Has the right delivery arrived?

Uses example figures: the numbers marked (example figure) or (example figures) are made up to show the method.

Counting stock is where shop staff use maths most. A quick estimate catches a wrong delivery before you sign for it. 19 cases of 24 tins arrive (example figures).

  1. Estimate: \(20 \times 24 = 480\).
  2. Exact: \(19 \times 24 = 456\). Close to the estimate, so the count looks right.

The answer: \(19 \times 24 = 456\) tins

Practise it

Games on MaffsGames that practise estimation and rounding:

  • Estimation Golf: Estimate answers by rounding: the closer you get, the further the ball goes.
  • Estimation Engine: Round each number to 1 significant figure, then work out the estimate and see how far it is from the exact answer.
  • Fermi Lab: Break a big estimation question into smaller steps and estimate each one.

Sources

Every job and every figure that is not an example comes from a public page you can check.
